sources.note: sec.4.2.1 p.199, family-level: Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed, and in some languages they may harmonize with the nouns to which they are attached (Chen 1993)'. sources.note: Nothing. Gaopo (Jiading) entry is a bare inventory: 61 initials, 18 finals, 8 tones (24 55 13 31 43 22 43 55). No 重音/轻声 remark (whereas e.g. the Jiongnai paragraph on p.40 does say '轻声不明显'), so silence here is genuine.

sources.citation: Wang Fushi 王辅世 (ed.). 1985. 苗语简志 Miaoyu jianzhi [A sketch of the Miao language]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.105 lists 惠水次方言 北部土语 (c.50,000; Gaopo, Yangchang, Tangbao, Pingfa); pp.135/139 name 甲定 (贵阳市高坡) as the Huishui representative point but use it only for lexical/grammatical comparison; phonology chapter covers Dananshan only; the sole 轻声 remark (p.12) is about Layiping (Xiangxi) prefixes. Silent on stress for Jiading.

'A brief description of the Miao language' [苗语概况, Zhongguo Yuwen 1962(1)], and 'Chinese loanwords in Miao', English translations in Purnell, Herbert C. (ed.) 1972. Miao and Yao Linguistic Studies. sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey point (5) Chia ting 甲定, Hui shui hsien. p.5-6 item 11: in the northern subdivisions of the Huishui subdialect prefixes harmonize with the root final (qa13 ʔta24 'stone', qo13 plho24 'hail'); pp.56-59 Chia ting tone values 24 55 13 31 for tones 1-4. The word 'stress' never occurs. Silent.
